config.title: Berlin Opera for First-Time Visitors - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers on choosing a Berlin opera house, checking the current venue and planning a first evening.

items.q: Which Berlin opera house is best for a first-time visitor?
items.a: There is no universal best house. Choose Staatsoper Unter den Linden when you want a Mitte evening around Unter den Linden and Museum Island. Choose Deutsche Oper when your day is already in Charlottenburg or City West. Choose Komische Oper when the particular production appeals and you have checked its current listed venue.

items.q: Where does Komische Oper Berlin perform now?
items.a: Komische Oper Berlin lists Schillertheater, Bismarckstraße 110, 10625 Berlin as a current main venue. Its official venue page says the company has used Schillertheater since the 2023/24 season. Check the individual production page before you leave because a performance can use another location.

items.q: Does Staatsoper Unter den Linden have English surtitles?
items.a: The Staatsoper FAQ says it offers German and English surtitles on displays above the stage. It also says those displays are not readable from every seat, particularly some side parquet seats and rear lateral balcony rows, so check the official seating information if subtitles matter to you.

items.q: Are Berlin opera performances in English?
items.a: Do not assume that from the venue name or the English-language booking page. Open the individual production page and check the stated performance language and surtitles for the exact date and cast you are considering.

items.q: How should I plan an opera evening in Berlin?
items.a: Save the exact venue address from the production page, choose the nearby part of Berlin for your afternoon, and leave enough time to enter calmly. Treat Staatsoper as a Mitte evening and Deutsche Oper or Komische Oper at Schillertheater as west-Berlin evenings unless the live listing says otherwise.
